GateBench / Research artifact / v0.1

Can you trust the score?

A controlled audit of what tool-agent graders accept, what they miss, and which valid alternatives they reject.

SCRIPTED CONTROLS · SYNTHETIC WORKFLOWS
ResultsInspect controlsMethod
72
Task instances
1,560
Executed controls
432
Valid controls
1,128

This is a verifier regression study, not a model leaderboard. Labels come from independently specified workflow obligations. No model capability, intent, or real-world exploit rate is inferred.

Two ways a grader can be wrong

False acceptance counts invalid controls that pass. False rejection counts valid controls that fail. Points are observed rates; bars show 95% case-cluster bootstrap intervals.

What each grader sees

transcript
Trusts a completion claim in the final response.

goal
Checks requested final fields without the full preservation contract.

final_state
Checks goal and unrelated-state preservation, without action-time policy or replay.

exact_trace
Requires the canonical action plan, including its ordering.

hardened
Checks outcome, state preservation, action-time policy and evidence consistency.

no_history
Ablation: removes action-time policy checks.

no_frame
Ablation: removes unrelated-state preservation checks.

no_replay
Ablation: removes independent evidence-consistency checks.

Method and limits

  • Paired case clusters. 2,000 bootstrap draws, seed 17. A draw resamples whole task IDs with all their sibling probes. Estimates are episode-weighted ratios of counts. Family slices show point estimates only.
  • Curated control frequencies. Aggregate rates depend on how often each mutation appears in this corpus. The intervals describe sensitivity to the generated task mix; they do not estimate real-world agent failure rates.
  • Public procedural splits. Splits: dev, eval. The eval split changes parameters and includes designated composition probes. Public generators and labels are not a secret or contamination-proof holdout.
  • Executable violations and evidence corruption are separate. These controls change actual tool actions. Serialized input-corruption tests belong to a separate integrity suite.
  • Consistency is not authenticity. Independent replay checks recorded state transitions and evidence consistency. It does not authenticate a wholesale coherent forgery or secure a compromised runner. The trusted runner must own journal collection.
  • Bounded claims. Zero observed error means these specified controls passed. It does not prove verifier completeness or general resistance to reward hacking. No model result or intentional exploit is implied.
